Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Compare the differential genes on global proteome level and glycoproteome level for IPMN vs ND.  Provide a pathway level summary of biological functions of upregulated or downregulated glycopeptides whose global protein expression remained unchanged.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The user‐provided data comprise two paired comparisons of IPMN versus normal duct (ND) tissues from Wang et al. (2025): a global proteome (Table S2A, Uniprot‐mapped log2FC and FDR for 9,417 proteins) and a glycoproteome (Table S3I, site‐resolved glycopeptide log2FC and FDR for 85 glycopeptides). We focused on glycopeptides with significant up‐regulation (FDR ≤ 0.05 and “Up.Sig”) whose parent proteins showed no significant global abundance change (FDR > 0.05 or no Up/Down flag). This yielded six genes: ADAM10, CPD, DDAH1, ERLIN2, MPZL1, and TSPAN13.  

Keywords  
• IPMN × ND  
• Glycosylation/glycoproteome  
• Global proteome unchanged  
• NOTCH signaling  
• Sterol/sterol biosynthesis  

Candidate Genes  
ADAM10, CPD, DDAH1, ERLIN2, MPZL1, TSPAN13  

Pathway Enrichments (ORA, glyco-Up only; ORA p ≤ 0.05, gene sets: GO_BP_2023 & Reactome_2024)  

KEGG_2016 (UP)  
| Theme | Direction | Leading Genes |  
| (none at p≤0.2) | Up | — |  

GO_Biological_Process_2023 (UP)  
| Theme                                                                       | Direction | Leading Genes |  
| Regulation Of Cellular Response To Hypoxia (GO:1900037)                     | Up        | DDAH1          |  
| Citrulline Metabolic Process (GO:0000052)                                    | Up        | DDAH1          |  
| Arginine Catabolic Process (GO:0006527)                                      | Up        | DDAH1          |  
| SREBP Signaling Pathway (GO:0032933)                                         | Up        | ERLIN2         |  
| Regulation Of Sterol Biosynthetic Process (GO:0106118)                       | Up        | ERLIN2         |  

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP)  
| Theme                                                                     | Direction | Leading Genes |  
| Constitutive Signaling by NOTCH1 t(7;9)(NOTCH1 M1580 K2555) Translocation  | Up        | ADAM10        |  
| Signaling by NOTCH1 t(7;9)(NOTCH1 M1580 K2555) Translocation              | Up        | ADAM10        |  
| NOTCH4 Activation and Transmission of Signal to the Nucleus               | Up        | ADAM10        |  
| eNOS Activation                                                           | Up        | DDAH1         |  
| Activated NOTCH1 Transmits Signal to the Nucleus                          | Up        | ADAM10        |  

Analysis  
Upregulated glycopeptides whose parent proteins were unchanged implicate distinct post-translational modulation of the secretory and signaling machinery. Notch pathway activation (ADAM10) and processing (Protein Maturation co-enrichment, CPD) emerge as top themes, suggesting enhanced juxtacrine signaling in IPMN epithelium. DDAH1 drives arginine/NO metabolism and hypoxia response, hinting at microenvironmental adaptation. ERLIN2’s link to sterol biosynthesis and SREBP signaling suggests altered membrane lipid homeostasis. MPZL1 and TSPAN13 glycosylation may affect cell adhesion and tetraspanin‐mediated trafficking. In contrast, the global proteome upregulated signature is dominated by immunoglobulin variable chains and lymphoid markers, highlighting a stromal or immune component not recapitulated by the glycoproteome subset.  

Targeted (Keyword-Guided) Subset  
• NOTCH (Reactome_Pathways_2024): All four NOTCH1/4–related terms (ADAM10) underscore preferential glycosylation of the metalloprotease that cleaves Notch receptors.  
• Sterol (GO_BP_2023): ERLIN2 re-glycosylation aligns with “Regulation Of Sterol Biosynthetic Process”, suggesting Golgi/Lipid raft remodeling.  
• Hypoxia/NO (GO_BP_2023; Reactome): DDAH1 enrichment in hypoxia and eNOS activation processes highlights glycosylation‐driven regulation of nitric oxide signaling.  

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
Up  
| Gene    | Role/Function                                     | Pathway(s)                                           |  
|---------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|  
| ADAM10  | Notch ectodomain sheddase; activates Notch signaling | Constitutive/Activated NOTCH1, NOTCH4, Protein Maturation |  
| DDAH1   | Arginine metabolism; regulates nitric oxide levels | Hypoxia response, Arginine/NO metabolism, eNOS Activation |  
| ERLIN2  | Endoplasmic reticulum lipid raft component         | SREBP signaling, Sterol biosynthesis                  |  
| CPD     | Carboxypeptidase; pro‐protein processing           | Protein Maturation, Protein Processing                |  
| MPZL1   | Cell‐adhesion receptor–like; Ig‐like glycoprotein  | (Not in top‐5 ORA tables; lower‐ranked adhesion terms) |  
| TSPAN13 | Tetraspanin family; membrane organization          | (Not in top‐5 ORA tables; potential receptor clustering) |  

Down  
| (none) | No significantly downregulated glycopeptides with unchanged proteome were observed. | — |

Comparisons  
Unlike the global proteome (immune-related Ig chains), the glycoproteome subset pinpoints intrinsic epithelial adaptations—especially in signaling (Notch), lipid metabolism, and NO homeostasis—independent of bulk protein abundance changes.  

Implications  
These findings suggest that site‐specific glycosylation fine-tunes key pathways in IPMN pathobiology—Notch activation, lipid raft assembly, and vascular/oxidative homeostasis—potentially offering glyco-targeted biomarkers or therapeutic angles distinct from total protein levels.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate altered glycosylation of ADAM10 and its effect on Notch cleavage and downstream transcription in IPMN organoids.  
2. Quantify sterol species and assess SREBP activity in IPMN versus ND to link ERLIN2 glycosylation with lipid flux.  
3. Examine DDAH1 glyco-isoforms’ impact on NO production and cyst fluid vascular permeability.  
4. Confirm MPZL1 and TSPAN13 glycan structures and evaluate their roles in epithelial adhesion and cyst integrity.
